title: Uplift Sprint: Proposal Templates & Renewal Tracker
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects modular proposal language, a compact QBR agenda tweak for signal-to-opportunity mapping, and a lightweight renewal tracker focused on upsell paths: Dedicated upgrades, Private deployments, and premium SLA add-ons. 

Audience and use cases:
- CS AEs running QBRs for mid-market and enterprise accounts.
- Renewal and expansion pods prepping outreach sequences.
- Solutions Eng and Sales engineering for technical objections.

Quick notes / constraints (scratch):
- Keep talk tracks < 10 min for executive QBRs.
- Always map to unit economics: $/token or $/concurrent-slot depending on customer posture.
- Flag regulated data / legal blockers early for Private path.

1) QBR micro-agenda (10–25 min variant) — insert at start of QBR deck
- 0–2 min: One-line health snapshot (usage, errors, latency, spend vs budget).
- 2–6 min: Customer outcomes (product metrics driven by LLMs: CTR, completions, reduction in manual work).
- 6–12 min: Signal-to-opportunity map (these are the concrete upsell levers we can pull).
  - Capacity risk (CI: rising queuing, tail latency spikes) => Dedicated upgrade suggestion
  - Data sovereignty / compliance need => Private deployment path
  - Cost predictability / premium uptime need => SLA add-on
- 12–18 min: Proposal options (short bullets + implications).
- 18–22 min: Next steps & decision map (who owns PoC, timeline, blockers).
- 22–25 min: Parking lot / technical follow-ups.

2) Signal definitions (so AEs and SREs agree on triggers)
- Capacity risk: sustained 95th latency > SLO for > 3 days OR queuing depth > threshold for two high-traffic windows.
- Cost unpredictability: month-to-month cost variance > 25% with no quota guardrails.
- Data residency requirement: new legal ask for data not to leave region or to be within customer VPC.
- Security/compliance escalation: need for SOC2+/ISO artifacts or HSM/KMS integration on a timeline.

3) Short proposal language (modular snippets you can paste into outreach or slides)
- Dedicated upgrade (executive summary):
  "Recommendation: Move to Redwood Dedicated to secure reserved GPU capacity with predictable per-token economics and an SLA-backed latency commitment. This reduces tail latency and eliminates burst contention during peak processing windows."
- Private deployment (executive summary):
  "Recommendation: Transition to Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) to meet data residency and regulatory controls. Private removes cross-tenant exposure and enables on-prem HSM integration for key material."
- Premium SLA add-on (executive summary):
  "Recommendation: Add Premium SLA to receive 24/7 incident response, priority capacity reservations, and a formal uptime/latency warranty tailored to your agreed traffic profile."

4) Pricing heuristics and levers (talk track only, not final pricing)
- Dedicated: show example math: baseline hosted spend $X/month. Dedicated reserved tier (N GPUs) -> effective $/inference decreases by ~30–60% depending on utilization. Include note on minimum commit and burst buffer pricing.
- Private: one-time platform fee + O&M (if managed) or license + install (if air-gapped). Expect longer lead time and security-review cadence.
- SLA: premium add-on as % uplift (typical 10–25%) depending on response time, capacity reservations.

5) Renewal & Upsell tracker (compact table for AE use — copy into sheet)
Columns (CSV-friendly):
- account, ae, ARR, renewal_date, current_product, usage_signal, proposed_path, proposal_date, owner_se, poc_start, budget_confirmed, blockers, status_notes
Example row:
- "Acme Retail, Aisha P., $120k, 2025-04-30, hosted-api, tail-latency, dedicated, 2025-01-15, Marco R., 2025-02-05, TBD, needs legal for data residency"

6) Outreach sequences & templates (short)
- Executive email (to sponsor):
  Subject: Quick note ahead of QBR — capacity/uptime options
  Body: "We’ve observed [signal]. To avoid product impact and stabilize unit cost, we have two straightforward options: (1) Reserved Dedicated, delivering predictable throughput and cost, or (2) Premium SLA to prioritize capacity and reduce incident windows. Can we schedule 20 min in the week after the QBR to review cost/impact math?"
- Technical email (to SRE/architect):
  Subject: Tech check: queueing & kv-cache behavior on current model
  Body: "Can you share current 95th% latency and queue depth for the last 14 days? Also confirm if you have any region-specific residency constraints. I’ll loop in Marco from SE to map Dedicated sizing."

7) Objection handling (quick bullets)
- "It’s too expensive": run the example util math — show break-even at X% utilization.
- "We can’t move data": propose Private pilot (non-prod first) + KMS plan.
- "We don’t want vendor lock-in": show pinning/versioning, export/import guidance, and A/B rollback plan.

8) Tech handoff checklist (for SEs when PoC approved)
- initial infra intake form filled (region, VPC CIDR, KMS requirements)
- legal/compliance packet requested and logged (POC: timeframe)
- performance target doc (latency SLO, throughput) signed by AE + customer eng sponsor
- dev/test dataset staging instructions and sample throughput profile

9) Proposed timeline (example for a Dedicated upgrade PoC)
- week 0: decision and SOW signoff (AE + customer PO)
- week 1–2: SE intake, infra prep, sizing call
- week 3: deploy PoC capacity, smoke test
- week 4: soak load + acceptance criteria evaluation
- week 5: roll plan + cutover window scheduling

10) Risk register (short)
- Delay in legal review -> extend timeline, propose scoping to non-PHI data.
- Unexpected cost growth in hybrid model -> propose temporary quota guardrail and cost alerts.
- Model drift/regression after quantization -> include eval suite and rollback path.

11) Action items (current sprint — editable)
- AE: surface accounts with usage_signal=capacity risk by Mon EOD (Evelyn)
- SE: draft Dedicated sizing template for up to 3 baseline models (Marco)
- Finance: provide sample committed pricing tiers (Samir)
- CS Ops: seed tracker with top 25 accounts (Aisha)

Notes to self / WIP ideas:
- Consider adding a short calculator widget for AE use (sheet) to compute break-even quickly.
- Template language for purchase order and SOW should be validated with legal; add version control.
- Keep one slide per proposal option that fits an exec QBR — 3 bullets max.

Appendix: Snippets for slide copy (one-liners)
- "Dedicated: Reserved capacity to stabilize throughput and reduce per-call cost."
- "Private: Meets regional data controls with customer-managed networking and optional air-gapped install."
- "SLA+: Priority capacity reservations, guaranteed response windows, and tailored uptime SLAs."

-- end doc --

(If this looks useful I’ll convert tracker CSV into a shared sheet and add a short calculator tab. Feedback welcome — mark comments in Drive or ping in #cs-growth.)
